business: Cyra Health, a private PCOS and irregular-cycle tracking app (iOS, Android, web)
target: Women in the US, 18 to 40, with diagnosed or suspected PCOS and irregular cycles, who want to understand their symptoms and be taken seriously by a clinician
where: Online: App Store, Google Play and the web; found through search, PCOS communities and social media

segments.name: Student or early-career with irregular periods

behaviours.name: Uses Flo or Clue today
behaviours.how: Has logged in a mainstream period app for years; annoyed its predictions are always wrong for her.

behaviours.name: Privacy-wary
behaviours.how: Deleted a period app after the data-sharing news; reads privacy policies before installing anything health-related.

behaviours.name: Research-heavy
behaviours.how: Reads r/PCOS, studies and guidelines; distrusts wellness claims and wants sources.

behaviours.name: App fatigue
behaviours.how: Has tried several tracking apps and quit each within a few weeks; logging feels like homework.

behaviours.name: Free-only
behaviours.how: Never pays for apps; uses Apple Health or notes; cancels anything after the trial.

behaviours.name: Pays for help
behaviours.how: Already pays for a PCOS program, supplements or telehealth; will pay if it saves time with doctors.

objections: Apple Health or my current app already tracks this for free
Every app paywalls the useful part and keeps upselling me
Predictions never work for my irregular cycles
I don't trust a period app with my health data
I've quit tracking apps before; I won't keep logging
An app won't change what my doctor does
I don't want another AI chatbot giving me health advice
Is this just another weight-loss app in disguise?
habits: you have a doctor's appointment coming up and keep forgetting what happened between visits
you scroll r/PCOS or TikTok PCOS content a few nights a week
your last period was more than six weeks ago
you track your cycle in Flo but ignore its predictions
you take metformin or inositol and can't tell if it helps
you are tired of being told to just lose weight
